wu: Dream Catcher: Students write one dream on a slip of paper and put it in a 'dream jar'. Teacher draws one and asks 'If you could make this dream come true, what would you do?'
wuAlt: Alternative warm-up 1: Two Stars and a Wish - students share two real-life achievements and one wish using 'I wish I could...'
Alternative warm-up 2: Dream Lottery - students pick a dream card from a hat and discuss it in pairs
pres: Teacher shows a picture of a Moroccan desert camp and says 'If I were in the Sahara now, I would ride a camel'. Model 3-4 sentences with 'If I were... I would...'. Check understanding with thumbs up/down: 'If I were a bird, I would fly to the Atlas Mountains' - true or false for me?
presAlt: Alternative presentation 1: Dream Scenario Cards - teacher holds up a card 'Win 1 million dirhams' and models 'If I won 1 million dirhams, I would build a school in my village'
Alternative presentation 2: Realia - teacher shows a plane ticket and says 'If I had this ticket, I would visit New York to see the Statue of Liberty'
prac: Hypothetical Auction: Students get dream scenario cards (e.g., 'Speak English fluently', 'Meet a celebrity'). In groups, they 'bid' using 'If I could [dream], I would [action]'. Highest bidder explains their plan. Teacher monitors and corrects 'If I were' vs 'If I was'.
pracAlt: Alternative practice 1: Conditional Chain - students sit in a circle and each adds to the story: 'If I had a magic lamp, I would wish for... and if that happened, I would...'
Alternative practice 2: Dream Role Cards - students draw roles (e.g., 'You are a famous chef') and interview each other with 'If you were me, what would you cook?'
ls: Dream Interviews: Students listen to 3 short audio clips of people talking about their dreams (e.g., 'If I could travel anywhere, I would go to Japan'). They fill in a table: 'Dream', 'Action', 'Reason'. Teacher plays twice, then checks answers in pairs.
re: Dream Relay: After break, students stand in two lines. Teacher whispers a conditional sentence (e.g., 'If I were rich, I would buy a car') to the first student. They whisper it down the line. Last student says it aloud. First correct team wins.
prod: Dream Scenario Role Cards: Students pick a card (e.g., 'You are a tour guide in Oujda', 'You are a student studying abroad'). In pairs, they roleplay a conversation using 'If I were you, I would...'. They must give advice about achieving a dream. Teacher observes and takes notes.
rw: Wishes Paragraph: Students read a short text about a Moroccan's dream to open a business. They underline all 'I wish' sentences. Then, they write their own 80-word paragraph about their dream life, using at least 3 second conditionals and 2 'I wish' sentences.
st: Teacher tells a short story about a Moroccan who achieved their dream (e.g., starting a cooperative). End with: 'Today we imagined dreams using second conditionals. Thank you for sharing your ideas. Goodbye!'
g: Students bid for dream cards using 'If I could [dream], I would [bid]' - highest bidder wins the card
Students sit in a circle and each adds to a story using 'If I were... I would...'
Students roleplay giving advice about dreams using 'If I were you, I would...'
Students interview each other about dreams and fill in a table
Whisper a conditional sentence down a line - last student says it aloud
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a conditional dream poem (4 lines using 'If I were... I would...')
Support / weaker learners: Use a sentence frame 'If I were ___, I would ___' to complete 5 sentences
hw: Homework option 1: Write a 100-word email to a friend about your dream vacation using 3 second conditionals
Homework option 2: Record a 1-minute voice note describing your dream job using 'If I were a..., I would...'
Homework option 3: Draw a picture of your dream life and write 3 sentences about it using conditionals
tip: Use Moroccan cultural references (e.g., 'If I were in charge of the Sahara Festival, I would...') to make conditionals more relevant and engaging for learners.
